injuryReports.name: Kyle Dugger
injuryReports.returnComment: Dugger has missed the past three games, but he has a chance to get back on the field against Washington. The veteran safety has appeared in just four games this season, logging 10 tackles (five solo) and a pass breakup.
injuryReports.injury: Quadriceps

injuryReports.name: Dalton Risner
injuryReports.returnComment: Risner was held out of practice all week due to injuries to both of his knees that he sustained in Week 10 against the Steelers. Jalen Rivers figures to start at right guard Monday in the absence of Risner, whose next chance to play is Week 12 against the Saints on Sunday, Nov. 29.
injuryReports.injury: Knee

injuryReports.name: Dax Hill
injuryReports.returnComment: Hill was held out of practice all week while battling through an illness. He could still suit up Monday if he progresses enough in his recovery, but if he's not cleared to play, then Josh Newton, PJ Jules and DJ Ivey would all be in line for more snaps in the secondary.
injuryReports.injury: Illness

injuryReports.name: Andrei Iosivas
injuryReports.returnComment: Iosivas was a full participant in all three practices during Week 11 prep, but it looks like the fourth-year wide receiver will stay on injured reserve for at least one more week while recovering from a thumb injury. If he's inactive for Monday's game, then his next chance to play would be Week 12 against the Saints on Sunday, Nov. 29.
injuryReports.injury: Thumb

injuryReports.name: Joe Burrow
injuryReports.returnComment: Burrow dealt with an illness during Week 11 prep, but with no injury tag the 2020 first overall pick has been officially cleared to play Monday night -- and per ESPN.com he is confident he will do so at "full strength." He's thrown at least three touchdowns in each of his last five outings, and over that span he has completed 77.6 percent of his passes for 1,624 yards, 20 touchdowns and three interceptions while turning 13 carries into 47 yards and two scores. The Bengals will face a Commanders defense that ranks 31st in the NFL in passing yards allowed per game (244.8) and 30th in red-zone touchdown rate (71.9 percent).
injuryReports.injury: Burrow (illness) does not have an injury designation ahead of Monday's game against the Commanders.

injuryReports.name: Oren Burks
injuryReports.returnComment: Burks has been working through a groin issue for the past couple of weeks, and he aggravated the injury during the Bengals' 38-18 win over the Steelers on Sunday. His placement on IR means he'll be required to miss at least the next four games, so his next opportunity to play is Week 15 against the Panthers on Sunday, Dec. 20.
injuryReports.injury: Groin

injuryReports.name: Myles Hinton
injuryReports.returnComment: The offensive tackle came down with the illness last Sunday morning and had to miss the Bengals' win over the Steelers that night. Hinton seems to be over the illness, and he should be ready to resume his role as a reserve lineman Monday night against the Commanders.
injuryReports.injury: Hinton (illness) was a full participant in practice Thursday, Paul Dehner Jr. of The Athletic reports.

injuryReports.name: Swayze Bozeman
injuryReports.returnComment: The linebacker suffered a broken forearm in Week 5 against the Dolphins but now has a maximum of 21 days to get ready for a return to action. He played just one defensive snap across the first four games of the season but was a fixture on special teams.
injuryReports.injury: Forearm

injuryReports.name: Tee Higgins
injuryReports.returnComment: It's a new "injury" for Higgins, but the full participation level suggests it's nothing serious after the wideout was managed late in last Sunday night's blowout win over the Steelers, per Kelsey Conway of The Cincinnati Enquirer. Higgins already has a fantasy-friendly 53 catches (on 73 targets) for 824 yards and six touchdowns through nine games. He's on pace for a career year in 2026.
injuryReports.injury: Higgins (knee) was a full participant in Thursday's practice, Paul Dehner Jr. of The Athletic reports.

injuryReports.name: Dylan Fairchild
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable
injuryReports.injury: Oblique

injuryReports.name: Joe Flacco
injuryReports.returnComment: With the Bengals having built their lead to 20 by the midway point of the fourth quarter, head coach Zac Taylor pulled starter Joe Burrow from the contest and turned to Flacco to run down the clock in the win. The appearance was Flacco's third of the season, but the veteran signal-caller still has yet to attempt a pass.
injuryReports.injury: Flacco took the field for the Bengals' final possession of Sunday's 38-18 win over the Steelers, attempting no passes while handing off to running back Tahj Brooks on all three of his snaps.

injuryReports.name: Jordan Battle
injuryReports.returnComment: Battle ranked second on Cincinnati in stops. One of his six tackles went for a loss, and the 25-year-old also forced a fumble, though it was recovered by the Steelers. Battle has played every defensive snap in seven of the Bengals' nine contests this season, and he's collected 58 tackles and eight defensed passes, including three interceptions.
injuryReports.injury: Battle finished Sunday's 38-18 win over Pittsburgh with six tackles (four solo), one defensed pass and one forced fumble.

injuryReports.name: Demetrius Knight Jr.
injuryReports.returnComment: Knight led Cincinnati in tackles in the blowout win. The second-year linebacker has recorded exactly eight stops in four of his past five games, and he's finished with at least that tally in all but three of his appearances overall this season. Knight hasn't yet recorded a sack, but he's on pace to blow by his rookie total of 106 stops, as he has 71 tackles across nine games.
injuryReports.injury: Knight finished with eight tackles (six solo) and a defensed pass against the Steelers in a 38-18 victory Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Barrett Carter
injuryReports.returnComment: Carter's tackle tally tied for second-most on the Bengals. The second-year pro has now reached the six-tackle mark in all but one of his nine games this season. Carter leads the Bengals with 74 stops overall, and he's recorded 1.5 sacks, five defensed passes (including an interception) and two forced fumbles.
injuryReports.injury: Carter posted six tackles (two solo) and a defensed pass in Sunday's 38-18 win over Pittsburgh.

injuryReports.name: Drew Sample
injuryReports.returnComment: Sample entered the contest with no catches over his previous two games, but he tied season-high marks in both receptions and targets versus the Steelers. He gave Cincinnati a two-score lead just after the beginning of the second quarter when he hauled in a three-yard TD from Joe Burrow. Sample has two touchdowns over his past four games, but with just five catches for 39 yards during that span, he's almost entirely dependent on getting into the end zone to generate useful fantasy production.
injuryReports.injury: Sample caught all three of his targets for 15 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 38-18 win against Pittsburgh.

injuryReports.name: Evan McPherson
injuryReports.returnComment: McPherson converted a 24-yard field-goal attempt on the first drive of the game. The kicker proceeded to miss a 43-yarder in the second quarter of the contest, though the miss did not end up mattering to the final result of the game. McPherson is now 13-for-14 on field-goal attempts and 33-for-33 on PATs over nine contests this season.
injuryReports.injury: McPherson made one of his two field-goal attempts and all five PATs in the Bengals' 38-18 win over the Steelers on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Dohnte Meyers
injuryReports.returnComment: Meyers reeled in multiple passes for the third straight game, and he was able to secure his first score of the year in the second quarter on a 15-yard touchdown pass from Joe Burrow. The 26-year-old's 28 offensive snaps ranked fourth at wide receiver for Cincinnati behind Ja'Marr Chase (59), Tee Higgins (51) and Colbie Young (29). With Andrei Iosivas (thumb) nearing a return to action, Meyers may see a sharp drop in offensive opportunities in the near future.
injuryReports.injury: Meyers caught both of his targets for 20 yards and a touchdown while also adding 58 yards as a kick returner during Sunday night's 38-18 win over the Steelers.

injuryReports.name: Samaje Perine
injuryReports.returnComment: It looked like Chase Brown found the end zone in the fourth quarter for his third score of the game, but replay assist revealed that his knee came down just short of the goal line. Perine came in on the next play and took the ball for a one-yard touchdown to extend the Bengals' lead to 38-10 following Evan MacPherson's successful extra-point try. It was Perine's third touchdown of the season and first since Week 7 against the Ravens, and over his last five games, he has turned 39 carries into 151 yards (3.9 YPC) and two touchdowns while adding seven catches on as many targets for 44 yards and a score. He'll continue to operate as the Bengals' RB2 behind Brown heading into Week 11 against the Commanders on Monday, Nov. 23.
injuryReports.injury: Perine turned six carries into 14 yards and a touchdown and hauled in all four of his targets for 25 yards during the Bengals' 38-18 win over the Steelers on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Tahj Brooks
injuryReports.returnComment: All three of Brooks' carries came during the Bengals' final possession of the fourth quarter, when the team had already built a sizable lead and opted to rest multiple key players, including top running back Chase Brown. Brooks has been active for all nine of the Bengals' games to date but has logged just six carries, all of which have come late in blowout victories. So long as Brown and Samaje Perine are both available, Brooks will continue to see limited playing time on offense.
injuryReports.injury: Brooks carried three times for 12 yards while taking the field for three of the Bengals' 66 offensive snaps in Sunday's 38-18 win over the Steelers.

injuryReports.name: Mike Gesicki
injuryReports.returnComment: Gesicki caught six touchdowns in the first seven games of the season, but he's now produced just three grabs for 20 scoreless yards over the past two contests. The fluky touchdown rate was never going to hold up, and Joe Burrow funnels so many of his targets through Ja'Marr Chase, Tee Higgins and Chase Brown that there isn't a whole lot more to go around to Cincinnati's ancillary weapons. Gesicki is a touchdown-or-bust fantasy option most weeks despite running a bunch of routes as the de facto slot receiver.
injuryReports.injury: Gesicki caught one pass for nine yards in Sunday night's 38-18 win over the Steelers.

injuryReports.name: Chase Brown
injuryReports.returnComment: Brown averaged a solid 4.4 yards per carry, but as is customary, his rushing opportunities were capped in a Bengals offense that typically takes a pass-heavy approach irrespective of game script. He still benefited from that philosophy, however, as he tied his second-highest reception total on the season while ending his seven-game touchdown drought by hitting paydirt twice. Brown will get another favorable opportunity to build on his production in Week 11, when the Bengals travel to D.C. for a matchup with the Commanders.
injuryReports.injury: Brown rushed 10 times for 44 yards and brought in eight of nine targets for 39 yards for two touchdowns in the Bengals' 38-18 win over the Steelers on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Ja'Marr Chase
injuryReports.returnComment: Chase posted one of his signature 200-yard performances, with Sunday night's qualifying as the fourth of his storied career and marking his third instance accomplishing it against an AFC North rival. Needless to say, all three components of Chase's receiving line led the Bengals by a wide margin on the night as well, and after failing to hit the century mark in yardage in any of the first six games of the season, the star wideout has recorded at least 141 receiving yards in three straight. Chase is now up to a 64-878-7 line on 87 targets across nine games heading into a Week 11 Monday night home road matchup against the Commanders on Nov. 23.
injuryReports.injury: Chase brought in 11 of 14 targets for 231 yards in the Bengals' 38-18 win over the Steelers on Sunday night. He also committed a fumble that stayed with Cincinnati.

injuryReports.name: DJ Turner II
injuryReports.returnComment: Turner was able to play through his ankle injury in Week 9 against the Falcons, and it now looks like it's behind him entirely. He projects to start at cornerback against a pass-heavy Steelers offense Sunday.
injuryReports.injury: Turner (ankle) was a full participant at practice Thursday.

injuryReports.name: Cody Schrader
injuryReports.returnComment: Schrader's elevation is his third of the season, so he'll need to be signed to Denver's active roster in order to see game action for the team beyond Sunday. In his previous two appearances, the third-year pro played a total of two offensive snaps and nine snaps on special teams without recording any carries or targets. Schrader isn't likely to be much of a factor on offense Sunday against Las Vegas, as Jonah Coleman and J.K. Dobbins should continue to lead the Broncos' backfield. However, Schrader could contribute as a kick returner -- he's tallied 68 yards on three kickoff returns this season.
injuryReports.injury: The Broncos elevated Schrader from their practice squad to their active roster Saturday, Susanna Weir of the team's official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Taylor Rapp
injuryReports.returnComment: Rapp was cut from the Broncos' active roster in early November before opting to stick around as a member of the team's practice squad. His elevation gives Denver more depth in the secondary in the event that Brandon Jones (hamstring) cannot play against the Raiders on Sunday.
injuryReports.injury: The Broncos signed Rapp from the practice squad to the active roster Saturday, Zac Stevens of TheDNVR.com reports.

injuryReports.name: Talanoa Hufanga
injuryReports.returnComment: Hufanga logged three consecutive full practices during Week 11 prep. The strong safety did not let his persistent ankle injury inhibit him during the week, clearing him of any injury designation that may have followed him into Sunday's contest.
injuryReports.injury: Hufanga (ankle) does not have any injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Raiders, Aric DiLalla of the Broncos' official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Caleb Lohner
injuryReports.returnComment: The Broncos opened Lohner's 21-day practice window Wednesday. The tight end is not quite ready to make his season debut, as he is still tending to his recovery from a foot injury he sustained in the offseason. Lohner was a full participant in all three Week 11 prep sessions, meaning his odds of returning in Week 12 are quite good if he can continue to log full sessions.
injuryReports.injury: Foot

injuryReports.name: Riley Moss
injuryReports.returnComment: Moss was a full participant in Friday's practice. The newly extended Broncos starter has cleared the NFL's five-step concussion protocol and is all set to suit up for Sunday's contest. The team's Week 10 bye helped Moss rest and recover from the injury he sustained during the Broncos' Week 9 win over the Panthers.
injuryReports.injury: Moss (concussion) does not have any injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Raiders, Aric DiLalla of the Broncos' official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Brandon Jones
injuryReports.returnComment: Jones strung together three limited practices Week 11 prep, and he has a chance to return from a one-game absence due to a hamstring injury that he picked up in Week 8 against the Chiefs. JL Skinner figures to be the top candidate to start alongside Talanoa Hufanga at safety if Jones is not cleared to play against Las Vegas.
injuryReports.injury: Hamstring

injuryReports.name: Jaylen Waddle
injuryReports.returnComment: Waddle was limited to just 14 snaps and one catch for 22 yards before exiting the Broncos' Week 9 win over the Panthers with a concussion. Following a well-time Week 10 bye, Waddle has progressed through the NFL's concussion protocol, ensuring that Denver's top pass catcher -- who has recorded a 30/337/2 receiving line on 52 targets through nine contests -- will be available this weekend.
injuryReports.injury: Waddle (concussion) doesn't carry an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Raiders after practicing fully this week.

injuryReports.name: Kris Abrams-Draine
injuryReports.returnComment: The cornerback was a limited participant Wednesday. Abrams-Draine had to miss the Broncos' win over the Panthers in Week 9 ahead of the team's Week 10 bye. Now that he's had a week off to get healthy, he appears ready to play Sunday against Las Vegas.
injuryReports.injury: Abrams-Draine (ankle) practiced in full Thursday.

injuryReports.name: Adam Prentice
injuryReports.returnComment: It appears Prentice entered the league's concussion protocol following the Broncos' Week 9 win over the Panthers. He had additional time to recover courtesy of the Week 10 bye, so the veteran fullback should be available for Sunday's AFC West tilt against the Raiders.
injuryReports.injury: Prentice (concussion) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice.

injuryReports.name: Alex Singleton
injuryReports.returnComment: Singleton's six stops were a season low, but he still finished second on the Broncos in that category behind Jahdae Barron (eight). It's been a career year for Singleton, who is up to an NFL-leading 107 total tackles through nine regular-season games, which includes 2.0 sacks.
injuryReports.injury: Singleton recorded six tackles (two solo) during the Broncos' 26-21 win over the Panthers in Week 9.

injuryReports.name: Adam Trautman
injuryReports.returnComment: Trautman failed to record a catch across six games between Weeks 2 and 7, but he has logged two receptions in each of his two outings. His 41 offensive snaps ended up being ahead of fellow tight end Evan Engram (38), although the latter has been more involved in the Broncos' offensive game plan than Trautman. The Broncos' next game takes place in Week 11 against the Raiders on Sunday, Nov. 22.
injuryReports.injury: Trautman caught two of three passes for 15 yards during the Broncos' 26-21 win over the Panthers on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Marvin Mims Jr.
injuryReports.returnComment: Nineteen of Mims' 24 snaps came on offense, although he logged only two touches in the process. He hasn't seen more than four targets in a game this season, with most of his output coming on special teams as a returner on both kickoffs and punts. The Broncos are on a bye for Week 10, so their next game will take place in Week 11 against the Raiders on Sunday, Nov. 22
injuryReports.injury: Mims caught one of two targets for zero yards, added a five-yard carry and returned three punts for 22 yards during the Broncos' 26-21 win over the Panthers on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Troy Franklin
injuryReports.returnComment: Franklin drew a 27-yard pass interference penalty on the Broncos' second offensive play of the game, but the third-year wide receiver didn't log his first catch until early in the fourth quarter. He has operated in a rotational role for most of the season, and even with Jaylen Waddle in the league's concussion protocol, Franklin will likely maintain that workload following the Broncos' Week 10 bye.
injuryReports.injury: Franklin brought in three of four targets for 31 yards during the Broncos' 26-21 win over the Panthers on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Evan Engram
injuryReports.returnComment: The four catches matched Engram's season high, and his 33 yards were his most since Week 5. It goes without saying, but Engram is well off the fantasy radar at tight end. He has 17 catches for 169 yards and one touchdown through nine games, averaging a career-low 18.8 yards per contest.
injuryReports.injury: Engram caught four of five targets for 33 yards in Sunday's 26-21 win over the Panthers.

injuryReports.name: Wil Lutz
injuryReports.returnComment: Lutz's field-goal tries were good from 26 and 48 yards. The 32-year-old has now converted 16 of his 19 field-goal attempts and all 16 of his extra-point tries across nine appearances this season.
injuryReports.injury: Lutz went 2-for-2 on both his field-goal attempts and extra-point tries during Denver's win over Carolina on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: J.K. Dobbins
injuryReports.returnComment: Dobbins saw 13 fewer carries than rookie running back Jonah Coleman (17-57-1) in the game. The four rushes were a season low for Dobbins, and he figures to continue to operate as the team's No. 2 option in the backfield moving forward.
injuryReports.injury: Dobbins rushed four times for 18 yards and caught his only target for four yards during Sunday's 26-21 win over Carolina.

injuryReports.name: Pat Bryant
injuryReports.returnComment: Bryant was activated from IR on Saturday after recovering from an ankle injury, and he came up big late in Sunday's contest, hauling in a 26-yard TD strike from Bo Nix with less than six minutes left in the fourth quarter for what proved to be the game-winning score. The second-year wideout's clutch play came after Jaylen Waddle (concussion) had left the game, and if a Week 10 bye doesn't give him enough time to recover, Bryant could see an elevated role in Week 11 against the Raiders.
injuryReports.injury: Bryant caught four of five targets for 56 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 26-21 win over Carolina.

injuryReports.name: Courtland Sutton
injuryReports.returnComment: The five grabs and nine targets led the Broncos on the day, but Pat Bryant just edged him out for the receiving yards lead. The highlight of Sutton's solid performance was a three-yard TD from Bo Nix in the first quarter, as none of his receptions went for longer than 12 yards. Denver gets a well-timed bye in Week 10, but if Jaylen Waddle (concussion) isn't cleared to play on the other side of it, Sutton could see bigger volume in Week 11 against the Raiders. On the season, the long-time Bronco sports a 25-266-2 line on 46 targets through nine games.
injuryReports.injury: Sutton caught five of nine targets for 45 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 26-21 win over the Panthers.

injuryReports.name: Jonah Coleman
injuryReports.returnComment: The rookie has seized control of the lead-back role for the Broncos, with his 21 touches dwarfing J.K. Dobbins' five, and Coleman's nine-yard TD run early in the fourth quarter put his team in the lead for good. Coleman has piled up 261 scrimmage yards and two rushing touchdowns over the last three games, and there's no reason to think his role will shrink on the other side of a Week 10 bye.
injuryReports.injury: Coleman carried the ball 17 times for 57 yards and a touchdown and caught all four of his targets for 31 yards in Sunday's 26-21 win over the Panthers.

injuryReports.name: Bo Nix
injuryReports.returnComment: The Broncos had the home team right where they wanted them heading into the fourth quarter -- holding a lead -- and Nix worked his usual magic over the final 15 minutes, leading back-to-back touchdown drives capped by a nine-yard TD run from Jonah Coleman and a 26-yard strike to Pat Bryant for what proved to be the winning score. Nix did throw his first INT since Week 3 in the win, but he heads into a Week 10 bye with Denver riding a five-game win streak that has taken it to the top of the AFC West.
injuryReports.injury: Nix completed 25 of 37 passes for 237 yards and two touchdowns with one interception in Sunday's 26-21 win over the Panthers. He added two rushing yards on five carries.

injuryReports.name: Jordan Davis
injuryReports.returnComment: Acquired Nov. 9 in a deal with the Eagles, Davis didn't end up suiting up in the Jaguars' 40-23 win over the Titans last weekend while the Jacksonville coaching staff opted to give him more time to get acclimated to his new team. After a full week of practice, Davis should be ready to step into a starting role at defensive tackle.
injuryReports.injury: Davis is slated to make his Jaguars debut Sunday against the Giants, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.

injuryReports.name: Jessie Bates III
injuryReports.returnComment: Acquired Nov. 9 in a deal with the Falcons, Bates didn't end up suiting up in the Jaguars' 40-23 win over the Titans last weekend while the Jacksonville coaching staff opted to give him more time to get acclimated to his new team. After a full week of practice, Bates should be ready to step into a starting role at safety alongside Antonio Johnson.
injuryReports.injury: Bates is slated to make his Jaguars debut Sunday against the Giants, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.

injuryReports.name: Danny Striggow
injuryReports.returnComment: Striggow wasn't able to clear concussion protocol. He's appeared in nine games this season, logging 25 percent of the defensive snaps as a rotational defensive lineman.
injuryReports.injury: Concussion

injuryReports.name: B.J. Green II
injuryReports.returnComment: Green has strung together six consecutive full practices since being designated to return from injured reserve Nov. 11. He's not quite ready to be activated from IR, so his next chance to play is Week 12 against the Titans on Sunday, Nov. 29. Green is in the final stages of his recovery from an elbow injury that he suffered in Week 1 against the Browns.
injuryReports.injury: Forearm

injuryReports.name: Travon Walker
injuryReports.returnComment: Walker was a full participant in Friday's practice, and that was enough for the fifth-year defensive end to avoid an injury tag heading into Sunday's contest. The 2022 first-rounder has 22 tackles (10 solo), including 3.0 sacks, and two pass defenses through nine regular-season games.
injuryReports.injury: Walker (ribs) does not have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Giants.

injuryReports.name: Antonio Johnson
injuryReports.returnComment: Johnson was a limited participant in all three Week 11 practices, but the 2023 fifth-rounder has done enough to avoid an injury tag ahead of Sunday's contest. Johnson has accumulated 40 tackles (23 solo), including 1.5 sacks, and one pass defense across eight regular-season games.
injuryReports.injury: Johnson (ankle) does not carry an injury designation into Sunday's game against the Giants.

injuryReports.name: LeQuint Allen Jr.
injuryReports.returnComment: Allen has next to no fantasy appeal having played a total of 73 offensive snaps this season. In nine games, he's touched the ball a total of three times on offense.
injuryReports.injury: Allen (hamstring) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Giants.

injuryReports.name: Chris Rodriguez Jr.
injuryReports.returnComment: The backup running back has been dealing with the hand issue for weeks but continues to play through it. Rodriguez has averaged an underwhelming 3.9 yards per carry on 59 attempts this season, allowing Bhayshul Tuten to run away with lead-back duties in Jacksonville.
injuryReports.injury: Rodriguez (hand) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Giants.

injuryReports.name: Jakobi Meyers
injuryReports.returnComment: Meyers has been playing through the ankle injury for weeks, so his status was never in real doubt despite limited practices all week. The veteran wideout doesn't have a touchdown catch since Week 3 and has topped 65 receiving yards in a game just once all season. He's a low-floor, low-ceiling fantasy option.
injuryReports.injury: Meyers (ankle) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Giants.

injuryReports.name: Bhayshul Tuten
injuryReports.returnComment: Tuten was deemed limited at practice Wednesday and then was a non-participant Thursday. It remains to be seen how the Jaguars classify his participation (or lack thereof) in Friday's session, with added clarity on that front set to arrive via the team's upcoming injury report.
injuryReports.injury: Tuten (ankle/foot) was present for the stretching portion of Friday's practice before moving to a side field, Ryan O'Halloran of The Florida Times-Union reports.

injuryReports.name: Matt Dickerson
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable
injuryReports.injury: Neck

injuryReports.name: Robert Hainsey
injuryReports.returnComment: Jonah Monheim will draw the start at center in place of Hainsey, who exited this past Sunday's 40-23 win over the Titans due to a knee sprain, per Jeremy Fowler of ESPN.com. According to Fowler, Hainsey's knee injury isn't considered season-ending, but the veteran lineman is viewed as week-to-week and could be a candidate for injured reserve.
injuryReports.injury: Knee

injuryReports.name: Foyesade Oluokun
injuryReports.returnComment: Sunday was the third time in nine regular-season games that Oluokun played every single defensive snap and the second time that he reached double-digit tackles. His nine solo stops were a season high and most in a game since Week 1 of the 2024 season. Oluokun has accumulated 44 tackles (30 solo), including 2.0 sacks, over his last five outings.
injuryReports.injury: Oluokun finished Sunday's 40-23 win over the Titans with 10 tackles (nine solo).

injuryReports.name: Cam Little
injuryReports.returnComment: Little was able to make four field-goal tries for the second straight week, converting attempts from 46, 48, 36 and 40 yards in the contest. The kicker has now gone 18-for-20 on field-goal attempts, including 4-for-6 from 50-plus yards, over nine contests during the 2026 campaign.
injuryReports.injury: Little went 4-for-4 on field-goal attempts and made all four of his PATs during Sunday's 40-23 win over the Titans.

injuryReports.name: Travis Hunter
injuryReports.returnComment: Fifty-six of Hunter's 62 snaps Sunday came on defense, and that's where he made his biggest impact with a diving interception on a Cam Ward pass intended for Elic Ayomanor, and the Jaguars offense converted that takeaway into a field goal 10 plays later. Hunter's impact on both sides of the ball has been undeniable: he has 28 catches (on 45 targets) for 298 yards and a touchdown, along with 36 tackles (24 solo) and seven pass defenses (including three interceptions) through nine regular-season games. The Jaguars will hit the road for Week 11 against the Giants on Nov. 22.
injuryReports.injury: Hunter caught both of his targets for 16 yards, recorded a three-yard carry and contributed five tackles (three solo) and an interception during the Jaguars' 40-23 win over the Titans on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Josh Cameron
injuryReports.returnComment: Cameron gave the Jaguars a 14-point lead early in the fourth quarter when he hauled in a 25-yard touchdown pass from Trevor Lawrence. It was the rookie wideout's third touchdown of the campaign but his first since Week 3. Cameron's 67 receiving yards marked a career high, while his three receptions tied the most he's had as a pro. Cameron's propensity for finding the end zone (his three TDs have come on just 12 total catches) is appealing, but at this point he isn't getting enough volume to be a reliable week-to-week fantasy asset.
injuryReports.injury: Cameron caught all three of his targets for 67 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 40-23, Week 10 win over Tennessee. He also returned five kickoffs for 142 yards.

injuryReports.name: Brian Thomas Jr.
injuryReports.returnComment: The three catches tied his season high, while the four targets represented his biggest volume since Week 2. The Jaguars' decision not to deal Thomas at the trade deadline remains a curious one, as the third-year wideout simply doesn't have a significant role in Liam Coen's offense and might not step into one even if someone like Parker Washington got injured -- Josh Cameron was more productive Sunday on three targets and caught one of Trevor Lawrence's three TDs. Thomas will take a 13-146-2 line on 26 targets over nine games into a Week 11 tilt against the Giants.
injuryReports.injury: Thomas caught three of four targets for 29 yards in Sunday's 40-23 win over the Titans.

injuryReports.name: Parker Washington
injuryReports.returnComment: The 152 receiving yards were a new career high for Washington, and the fourth-year WR highlighted his big day with a two-yard TD toss from Trevor Lawrence in the first quarter to open the scoring. It's Washington's second game this season with 100-plus yards, and he'll take a 36-645-6 line on 64 targets through nine contests into a Week 11 tilt against the Giants.
injuryReports.injury: Washington caught seven of nine targets for 152 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 40-23 win over the Titans.

injuryReports.name: Trevor Lawrence
injuryReports.returnComment: It was another huge performance from the 27-year-old QB, as Lawrence set a new season high in passing yards and threw at least three TDs for the fifth time in nine games to begin the year. He spread the ball around again, as seven different Jaguars caught multiple passes and Parker Washington, Josh Cameron and Brenton Strange were all on the other end of scores. Lawrence will take a sharp 21:5 TD:INT into a Week 11 clash with the Giants.
injuryReports.injury: Lawrence completed 25 of 35 passes for 352 yards and three touchdowns with one interception in Sunday's 40-23 win over the Titans. He added 27 yards on four carries.

injuryReports.name: Brock Bowers
injuryReports.returnComment: Bowers was in and out of last Sunday's loss to the Seahawks before exiting for good after halftime due to an ankle injury. Head coach Klint Kubiak labeled Bowers day-to-day last Monday, and he then missed Wednesday's practice before being limited Thursday and Friday and entering the weekend listed as questionable. It appears Bowers' availability will be subject to a pregame warmup, after which his status will be clarified about 90 minutes before Sunday's 4:25 p.m. ET kickoff. Fellow TE Michael Mayer will get a boost in standing if Bowers is inhibited or sidelined.
injuryReports.injury: Ankle

injuryReports.name: Carter Runyon
injuryReports.returnComment: Las Vegas is bringing up Runyon due to Brock Bowers (ankle) being listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Broncos. Runyon appeared in 13 games with the Raiders last season but logged just 45 offensive snaps and caught only one pass for three yards. He's depth behind Michael Mayer and Ian Thomas.
injuryReports.injury: The Raiders elevated Runyon from the practice squad Saturday.

injuryReports.name: Folorunso Fatukasi
injuryReports.returnComment: Fatukasi was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice before downgrading to a DNP on Thursday. The defensive lineman capped off Week 11 prep with a full session Friday but remains questionable for Sunday's divisional bout. If Fatukasi cannot suit up, the absence of Tonka Hemingway (stinger) means Thomas Booker and Tim Keenan will likely start alongside nose tackle Adam Butler for Sunday's game.
injuryReports.injury: Toe

injuryReports.name: Tonka Hemingway
injuryReports.returnComment: Hemingway did not participate in any Week 11 prep sessions as he continues to deal with a stinger injury he likely suffered in the Raiders' Week 10 loss to the Seahawks. With Hemingway ruled out and Folorunso Fatukasi (toe) listed as questionable, Thomas Booker is currently the only healthy defensive end for the Raiders as they head into a divisional bout.
injuryReports.injury: Upper Body

injuryReports.name: Matt Gay
injuryReports.returnComment: Gay, who was limited Wednesday, logged a DNP on Thursday, but it looks like he'll work in some capacity to close out the week. Per Warren, the Raiders worked out three kickers with Gay injured, but it appears as though it's only Gay and practice-squad member Kansei Matsuzawa available to handle kicks at Friday's practice.
injuryReports.injury: Hip

injuryReports.name: Thomas Booker IV
injuryReports.returnComment: An ankle injury has sidelined Booker for each of the Raiders' last two games. However, his full session Wednesday indicates that he's recovered from his injury and on track to play in Sunday's AFC West tilt against the Broncos. Booker has accumulated 13 tackles (nine solo) across seven regular-season games.
injuryReports.injury: Booker (ankle) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice, Sam Warren of The Athletic reports.

injuryReports.name: Kwity Paye
injuryReports.returnComment: Paye made an early exit in the second half of Sunday's loss to the Seahawks with a neck injury. The linebacker did not return to the contest, but the issue does not seem to have been serious. Paye is healthy and appears ready to log consistent full practices throughout Week 11 prep.
injuryReports.injury: Paye (neck) was not listed on the Raiders' injury report Wednesday, Sam Warren of The Athletic reports.

injuryReports.name: Dont'e Thornton Jr.
injuryReports.returnComment: Thornton is healthy again after sitting out the team's Week 10 loss to the Seahawks due to a back injury. However, it is still unlikely that the 23-year-old plays in Sunday's matchup versus the Broncos, as Thornton had been a healthy scratch every week since returning from injured reserve in late October prior to Week 10.
injuryReports.injury: Thornton (back) was a full participant in Las Vegas' practice Wednesday, Sam Warren of The Athletic reports.

injuryReports.name: Jeremy Chinn
injuryReports.returnComment: Chinn continues to put up consistent tackling numbers, as he's now logged at least seven stops in six straight games. The veteran safety has played all but one of Las Vegas' defensive snaps this season. He's up to 72 tackles, including 1.0 sacks, two pass defenses (including one interception), two forced fumbles and two recovered fumbles through 10 contests.
injuryReports.injury: Chinn tallied seven tackles (three solo) in a loss to Seattle on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Quay Walker
injuryReports.returnComment: Walker, Nakobe Dean and Maxx Crosby all had eight tackles Sunday to co-lead the team. Walker added a fumble recovery on the second play of the game that helped set up a Raiders touchdown. The veteran linebacker has remained productive in his first season with Las Vegas following four years in Green Bay. Walker has 80 tackles, including 2.0 sacks, and two recovered fumbles though 10 contests on the campaign.
injuryReports.injury: Walker posted eight tackles (four solo) and recovered a fumble against Seattle in Sunday's Week 10 loss.

injuryReports.name: Nakobe Dean
injuryReports.returnComment: Dean tied for the team lead in stops with Maxx Crosby and Quay Walker. Nonetheless, the veteran linebacker saw his five-game streak of double-digit tackles come to an end. Dean did contribute his first recovered fumble of the season when he scooped up a ball that was turned over by Seattle QB Drew Lock in the fourth quarter. Dean is tied with Broncos linebacker Alex Singleton for the NFL lead with 107 tackles, though Denver has played one fewer game.
injuryReports.injury: Dean registered eight tackles (five solo) and recovered a fumble Sunday in a Week 10 loss to the Seahawks.

injuryReports.name: Maxx Crosby
injuryReports.returnComment: Crosby tied for the team lead with his season-high eight stops. Among those tackles, four went for a loss, including a fourth-quarter sack of Drew Lock. After registering just a half-sack over six games from Week 2 to Week 7, Crosby has since finished with exactly 1.0 sacks in each of his past three contests. He's at 5.0 sacks overall through 10 games as he seeks a fifth NFL campaign with double-digit sacks.
injuryReports.injury: Crosby finished Sunday's loss to Seattle with eight tackles (seven solo), including 1.0 sacks.

injuryReports.name: Jack Bech
injuryReports.returnComment: Bech was the favorite target of rookie first-overall pick Fernando Mendoza, who was making his first career start Sunday after the Raiders shipped Kirk Cousins to the Vikings at the Nov. 10 trade deadline. Bech's seven targets were a season high, but he mustered only two catches for his efforts, and he failed to connect on each of the last four passes he saw from Mendoza in the fourth quarter. The volume appears to be there for Bech, and he could take on a larger role offensively in Week 11 against the Broncos on Nov. 22 if star tight end Brock Bowers (ankle) is unable to play.
injuryReports.injury: Bech caught two of seven targets for 10 yards during the Raiders' 21-13 loss to the Seahawks on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Dareke Young
injuryReports.returnComment: Young has suited up in each of the Raiders' 10 games this season, but he's been deployed almost exclusively on special teams. He's seen single-digit snaps on offense in five straight games and has posted a collective 2-36-0 receiving line on three targets on the campaign.
injuryReports.injury: Young went without a target while playing one of the Raiders' 59 snaps on offense in Sunday's 21-13 loss to the Seahawks. He also brought back one kickoff for 29 yards.

injuryReports.name: Jalen Nailor
injuryReports.returnComment: Making his first NFL start, No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza was under siege throughout the afternoon, as a ferocious Seahawks defense sacked him six times and limited him to just 143 passing yards on 29 attempts. As a result, Nailor and the Raiders' other pass catchers were held quiet, with running back Ashton Jeanty (four receptions for 46 yards) being the only Las Vegas player to top two catches and 25 receiving yards. Though Mendoza will get some more favorable matchups over the Raiders' final seven games, Nailor will be difficult to count on for production. Even while Kirk Cousins served as the starting quarterback for Las Vegas before being traded to the Vikings last week, Nailor was limited to just 14 receptions for 122 yards and one touchdown on 28 targets through eight appearances.
injuryReports.injury: Nailor recorded one reception for minus-1 yard on four targets in Sunday's 21-13 loss to the Seahawks.

injuryReports.name: Dylan Laube
injuryReports.returnComment: Since earning seven touches in a Week 5 blowout loss to the Patriots, Laube has been an afterthought on offense. He's played just eight total offense snaps in the Raiders' ensuing five games, and Sunday marked the first time all season that he was limited exclusively to special teams.
injuryReports.injury: Laube played all 22 of his snaps on special teams in Sunday's 21-13 loss to the Seahawks and returned two kickoffs for 46 yards and one punt for zero yards.

injuryReports.name: Michael Mayer
injuryReports.returnComment: Jack Bech (seven targets) was the only Las Vegas player to see more than four targets in Fernando Mendoza's first career start. The rookie quarterback targeted 10 different players on his 29 attempts. With Kirk Cousins' efficiency off to Minnesota, Mayer is a low-floor TE2 for fantasy, but he could get a bit of a boost if Brock Bowers' ankle injury causes him to miss time.
injuryReports.injury: Mayer caught two of three targets for 16 yards in Sunday's 21-13 loss to the Seahawks.

injuryReports.name: Tre Tucker
injuryReports.returnComment: In Fernando Mendoza's first career start at quarterback, Tucker saw just 6.9 percent of the targets, while Jack Bech led the team with seven looks. Tucker looks like someone who won't be usable in fantasy until he shows some tangible chemistry with the young quarterback.
injuryReports.injury: Tucker caught one pass for nine yards on two targets in Sunday's 21-13 loss to the Seahawks.

injuryReports.name: Fernando Mendoza
injuryReports.returnComment: The Mendoza era in Las Vegas officially kicked off this week following the trade of veteran QB Kirk Cousins to the Vikings, and the rookie first overall pick unsurprisingly flashed at times while also stalling numerous drives by taking six sacks overall. On a positive note, Mendoza didn't turn the ball over, and he also recorded his first touchdown as a pro on a 10-yard run on the Raiders' opening offensive possession. He'll seek to build on the initial start of his career next Sunday at Denver.
injuryReports.injury: Mendoza completed 17 of 29 passes for 143 yards, no touchdowns and no interceptions and rushed six times for 22 yards and one TD during Sunday's 21-13 loss to the Seahawks.

injuryReports.name: Mike Washington Jr.
injuryReports.returnComment: Aside from a 25-carry outburst in Week 8 at the Jets, Washington has logged 54 rushes along with four catches in nine appearances, which amounts to 6.4 touches per game. Despite that number, he continues to eat into the overall backfield picture, as lead runner Ashton Jeanty failed to tally double-digit rushes for a fourth straight contest Sunday. Washington should retain a modest role alongside Jeanty next Sunday at Denver.
injuryReports.injury: Washington compiled eight rushes for 23 yards and secured his only target for four yards during Sunday's 21-13 defeat to the Seahawks.

injuryReports.name: Ladd McConkey
injuryReports.returnComment: McConkey, who didn't record any snaps during Week 9 action due to back spasms and then was inactive in Week 10, is officially listed as questionable by the Chargers after logging limited practices all week. While the wideout is on track to return to action versus New York, those considering McConkey in Week 11 fantasy lineups are still advised to verify his status once inactives are posted ahead of Sunday's 4:05 pm ET kickoff, given the tricky nature of back spasms.
injuryReports.injury: Back

injuryReports.name: Rodney Shelley
injuryReports.returnComment: Shelley was already ruled out for Sunday's game against the Jets due to an ankle injury. His placement on IR means he must miss at least the next four games, so his next opportunity to play is Week 15 against the 49ers on Thursday, Dec. 17. Shelley has contributed both on defense and special teams and has eight solo tackles and a pass defense across six regular-season games.
injuryReports.injury: Ankle

injuryReports.name: Trey Pipkins III
injuryReports.returnComment: Pipkins is still listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Jets, but his activation from injured reserve is a good sign for his availability. If he's cleared to play, then he would likely reclaim his starting role at left guard. Pipkins landed on IR in mid-September due to a knee injury.
injuryReports.injury: The Chargers activated Pipkins (knee) from injured reserve Saturday.

injuryReports.name: Bud Dupree
injuryReports.returnComment: Dupree also asked for a trade earlier in the season, but the Chargers have so far not granted his request. The veteran edge rusher has been limited to special teams over the Chargers' last two games and has yet to record a sack. If he's let go by the Chargers, then Dupree could garner interest from teams looking for a boost in the pass rush.
injuryReports.injury: Dupree requested his release from the Chargers earlier this week, Jeremy Fowler of ESPN.com reports.

injuryReports.name: Isas Waxter
injuryReports.returnComment: Waxter ended Week 11 prep with consecutive limited sessions after being a non-participant Wednesday. If Waxter cannot suit up for Sunday's game, Deane Leonard is set to be the only reserve cornerback behind starters Cam Hart, Donte Jackson and Tarheeb Still (ankle).
injuryReports.injury: Waxter (ankle) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Jets, Omar Navarro of the Chargers' official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Kendall Williamson
injuryReports.returnComment: Williamson ended Week 11 prep with consecutive DNPs. The strong safety remains sidelined with a calf injury he sustained in Week 8 against the Rams.
injuryReports.injury: Calf

injuryReports.name: Justin Eboigbe
injuryReports.returnComment: Eboigbe was unable to play against the Ravens this past Monday due to an ankle injury. He ended Week 11 prep with a full practice Friday, which was enough for him to avoid an injury tag ahead of Sunday's contest. His return means there will be less rotational snaps at defensive end for rookie fifth-rounder Nick Barrett.
injuryReports.injury: Eboigbe (ankle) does not have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Jets.

injuryReports.name: Tarheeb Still
injuryReports.returnComment: Still was added to Friday's practice report as a limited participant due to an ankle injury. His late addition to the injury report isn't a great sign ahead of Sunday's game, and if he's unable to play, then Deane Leonard and Genesis Smith would both be in line for more snaps in the Chargers' secondary.
injuryReports.injury: Ankle

injuryReports.name: Daiyan Henley
injuryReports.returnComment: Henley was unable to practice all week, and head coach Jim Harbaugh said Friday that the fourth-year linebacker has been working through knee soreness since Monday's win against the Ravens, per Alex Insdorf of BoltBeat.com. Denzel Perryman and Marlowe Wax figure to be the top candidates to start at inside linebacker alongside Del'Shawn Phillips in the absence of Henley, whose next chance to play is Week 12 against the Patriots on Sunday, Nov. 29.
injuryReports.injury: Knee

injuryReports.name: Brenen Thompson
injuryReports.returnComment: Thompson has been sidelined by a hamstring injury and has not seen regular-season action since Week 2 against the Raiders. If he's ruled out for Sunday's game, then the rookie fourth-rounder's next chance to play would be Week 12 against the Patriots on Sunday, Nov. 29.
injuryReports.injury: Hamstring

injuryReports.name: Omarion Hampton
injuryReports.returnComment: "Generally, my expecation is [Hampton] is our leading ball carrier every week.  ... I knew based on his last two practice weeks, we were feeling like he was going to have a breakout performance at any given time," McDaniel said Friday. That breakout game took place Monday against the Ravens, when Hampton turned 22 carries into a season-high 105 yards and a touchdown in a 23-20 win for the Chargers. With the Chargers getting extra time to rest, Hampton's stock is trending up heading into Week 12 against the Jets, whose defense ranks 30th in the NFL in rushing yards allowed per game (135.3) and 29th in rushing touchdowns allowed (13).
injuryReports.injury: Offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel told reporters Friday that his "expectation" is that Hampton is the lead back for the Chargers, Omar Navarro of the team's official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Charlie Kolar
injuryReports.returnComment: The tight end is still in the concussion protocol, so he'll be up against it to clear the final hurdles, especially after the Chargers played Monday night against Baltimore. If Kolar is ruled out, David Njoku and Oronde Gadsden should handle most of the tight-end duties for the Bolts.
injuryReports.injury: Kolar (concussion) is questionable for Sunday's game against the Jets.

injuryReports.name: Dalvin Tomlinson
injuryReports.returnComment: In a game where Ravens quarterback Jacoby Brissett dropped back 51 times, there were no shortage of opportunities for the Chargers to rush the passer, and Tomlinson came away with the best single-game sack total of his nine-plus year career so far. He has taken on a larger role on the defensive line than 2025 third-rounder Jamaree Caldwell in recent weeks, and only Teair Tart played as many snaps on the Chargers' defensive front as Tomlinson did (36) in Week 10.
injuryReports.injury: Tomlinson recorded five tackles (three solo) including 2.0 sacks during Monday's 23-20 win at Baltimore.

injuryReports.name: Del'Shawn Phillips
injuryReports.returnComment: Phillips was in the right place at the right time when a Jacoby Brissett pass bounced off the helmet of rookie wideout Ja'Kobi Lane in the second quarter, and the turnover set up a Chargers touchdown that put the team ahead 17-7. His tackle total was also his highest going back to Week 18 of the 2023 season with the Ravens. With that said, his role in the Chargers' defense is still not big enough to warrant IDP consideration in most formats.
injuryReports.injury: Phillips recorded nine tackles (four solo) and an interception during Monday's 23-20 win at Baltimore.

injuryReports.name: Cameron Dicker
injuryReports.returnComment: Dicker's longest field goal on the day was only from 38 yards out, but his accuracy played a big part in the Chargers picking up their first win of the season. He hasn't missed a kick since Week 3, but the team's general inability to move the ball consistently keeps him from projecting as a top-tier fantasy option in most formats going into a Week 11 matchup versus the Jets.
injuryReports.injury: Dicker made all three of his field-goal tries and converted both of his extra-point attempts during Monday's 23-20 win at Baltimore.

injuryReports.name: David Njoku
injuryReports.returnComment: Njoku's snap count was predictably capped as he returned from a six-game absence due to a fibula injury that he sustained in Week 2 against the Raiders. His 19 offensive snaps were actually ahead of Oronde Gadsden (12), with Charlie Kolar leading all Chargers tight ends with 41 snaps on offense. With another week under his belt to get back up to speed, Njoku could be more involved in the Chargers' passing attack in Week 11 against the Jets on Sunday.
injuryReports.injury: Njoku played 19 offensive snaps but didn't get a target during Monday's 23-20 win over the Ravens on Monday.

injuryReports.name: Oronde Gadsden
injuryReports.returnComment: Gadsden went to the locker room during the first half of Monday's game after being poked in the ye, but the second-year tight end was cleared to return for the second quarter. However, his 12 offensive snaps were his lowest since Week 1 against the Cardinals (10), and that lack of playing time coincided with the return of veteran tight end David Njoku, who missed the Chargers' six prior games while on IR due to a fibula injury. Njoku and Charlie Kolar appear to be the Chargers' top options at tight end, squeezing Gadsden out of the game plan ahead of Week 11 against the Jets on Sunday.
injuryReports.injury: Gadsden hauled in his lone target for seven yards in Monday's 23-20 win over Baltimore.

injuryReports.name: Kimani Vidal
injuryReports.returnComment: Vidal's 15 offensive snaps were just ahead of Keaton Mitchell's 13, but both running backs took a back seat to Omarion Hampton, who was on the field for 36 of the Chargers' 57 snaps on offense and led the backfield with 22 carries for 105 yards and one touchdown. Vidal's two carries were his fewest since Week 3 against the Bills (one), although his 15-yard catch early in the third quarter set the Chargers up just outside the red zone, with Cameron Dicker connecting on a 34-yard field goal four plays later. Vidal and Mitchell appear to be falling into rotational roles behind Hampton heading into Week 11 against the Jets on Sunday.
injuryReports.injury: Vidal turned two carries into zero yards, brought in both of his targets for 14 yards and returned one kickoff for 32 yards during the Chargers' 23-20 win over the Ravens on Monday.

injuryReports.name: Keaton Mitchell
injuryReports.returnComment: One of Mitchell's carries went for 11 yards, but his other two rushes went for minus-five and minus-two yards, and all of those touches came on the same drive in the second quarter. His 13 offensive snaps were third-most among Chargers running backs behind Kimani Vidal (15) and Omarion Hampton (36), and it was Hampton that commanded the majority of backfield touches, finishing with 22 carries for 105 yards and a touchdown. Mitchell has logged four carries or fewer in three of his last four outings, and he'll continue to operate in a rotational role on offense heading into the Chargers' Week 11 home tilt against the Jets on Sunday.
injuryReports.injury: Mitchell turned three carries into four yards, failed to haul in his lone target and returned two kickoffs for 30 yards during the Chargers' 23-20 win over the Ravens on Monday.

injuryReports.name: Quentin Johnston
injuryReports.returnComment: The speedster was poised to see some added involvement with Ladd McConkey (back) sidelined, but that never materialized on a night when 86 of Justin Herbert's 129 passing yards went to Tre' Harris. Johnston's yardage total was a season-low figure, and he's now been limited to one reception in four of the last five games. Johnston's often been able to offset the modest catch totals with big plays, but that clearly wasn't the case Monday night. Johnston will remain a hit-or-miss fantasy option in a Week 11 home matchup against the Jets on Sunday, irrespective of McConkey's availability.
injuryReports.injury: Johnston brought in his sole target for six yards in the Chargers' 23-20 win over the Ravens on Monday night.

injuryReports.name: Tre' Harris
injuryReports.returnComment: With Ladd McConkey (back) sidelined, Harris functioned as a de facto top target for Justin Herbert, and he was responsible for all but 43 of his quarterback's passing yards. The yardage tally also was a career-high figure for Harris, who generated team-high totals with all three components of his receiving line. Harris is up to a career-high 348 receiving yards on 26 catches heading into a favorable Week 11 home matchup against the Jets on Sunday.
injuryReports.injury: Harris secured all five targets for 86 yards in the Chargers' 23-20 win over the Ravens on Monday night.

injuryReports.name: Justin Herbert
injuryReports.returnComment: Herbert ironically compiled his second-fewest passing yards of the season in the Chargers' first victory, but the talented signal-caller leaned heavily on both his legs and an effective rushing performance from Omarion Hampton. Herbert made a significant contribution himself to cap off Los Angeles' opening drive of the game, taking off when he couldn't find anyone open and recording a 22-yard rushing touchdown for the first points of the night. The game also marked Herbert's first interception-free performance of the season and gives the beleaguered Chargers' air attack something to hang its collective hat on heading into a favorable Week 11 home matchup against the Jets on Sunday.
injuryReports.injury: Herbert completed 12 of 18 passes for 129 yards with no touchdowns or interceptions and rushed seven times for 51 yards and a touchdown in the Chargers' 23-20 win over the Ravens on Monday night.

injuryReports.name: Kayode Awosika
injuryReports.returnComment: Awosika will suit up Monday for the first time since Week 2, when he suffered an injury to his fibula. He should slide back into his starting role at left guard.
injuryReports.injury: Awosika (fibula) is active for Monday's game against the Ravens.

injuryReports.name: Branson Taylor
injuryReports.returnComment: Taylor is battling an ankle injury and was ruled out for the Week 10 meeting with Baltimore. Now on injured reserve, he will be required to miss at least four games before being eligible to return.
injuryReports.injury: Ankle

injuryReports.name: Gavin Bartholomew
injuryReports.returnComment: Bartholomew was targeted four times in Week 10 for three catches, 36 yards and a touchdown in the Vikings' 30-10 win over the Packers. The tight end received more than one target in only one other game this season, Week 5, when Hockenson went down after two offensive snaps. While Bartholomew has proven himself a red-zone threat, Hockenson should return to seeing most of the tight end volume in Sunday's contest.
injuryReports.injury: Bartholomew should revert to a backup role with T.J. Hockenson returning from a wrist injury for Sunday's game against the 49ers, Craig Peters of the Vikings' official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Jeshaun Jones
injuryReports.returnComment: Jones -- who was managing a shoulder injury during Week 11 prep -- was a full participant in Friday's session, which was enough for him to avoid an injury tag for Sunday's contest. He was signed to the Vikings' 53-man roster Wednesday to give the team more depth at wide receiver while Jordan Addison recovers from a thumb injury. Jones figures to be limited to a rotational role on offense while serving as a contributor on special teams.
injuryReports.injury: Jones (shoulder) does not have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the 49ers in Mexico City.

injuryReports.name: Isaiah Rodgers
injuryReports.returnComment: Rodgers popped up on Thursday's practice report as a limited participant due to a quad injury. His practice reps were also limited in Friday's session, and his status for Sunday's contest may not be officially known until the Vikings announce their list of inactive players approximately 90 minutes before the 8:20 p.m. ET kickoff. Rookie fifth-rounder Charles Demmings and Zemaiah Vaughn would likely be the top candidates to start opposite James Pierre if Rodgers is not cleared to play against San Francisco.
injuryReports.injury: Quadriceps

injuryReports.name: Andrew Van Ginkel
injuryReports.returnComment: Van Ginkel's practice reps were limited Wednesday and Thursday while managing a quadriceps injury that he sustained in Week 10 against the Packers. He was a full participant in Friday's session, which was enough for the veteran edge rusher to avoid an injury tag for Sunday's contest. In Van Ginkel's four outings since the Vikings' Week 6 bye, he has accumulated 14 tackles (eight solo), including 4.5 sacks, one forced fumble and one fumble recovery.
injuryReports.injury: Van Ginkel (quadriceps) does not carry an injury designation into Sunday's game against the 49ers in Mexico City.

injuryReports.name: Blake Cashman
injuryReports.returnComment: Cashman will end up missing one game (Week 10 against the Packers) while in the league's concussion protocol, and his return means Ivan Pace will revert to a rotational role at inside linebacker for Sunday's contest. Cashman has accumulated 76 tackles (41 solo), including a career-high-tying 4.5 sacks, seven pass defenses and one fumble recovery across eight regular-season games.
injuryReports.injury: Cashman (concussion) does not carry an injury designation into Sunday's game against the 49ers in Mexico City.

injuryReports.name: Kyler Murray
injuryReports.returnComment: The quarterback lost his job to Kirk Cousins and will continue to manage a hamstring injury. Murray's availability will only matter moving forward if something happens to Cousins, either performance or injury related. Carson Wentz and Max Brosmer remain on the 53-man roster as backup options.
injuryReports.injury: Hamstring

injuryReports.name: T.J. Hockenson
injuryReports.returnComment: After sitting out last Sunday against Green Bay and then logging limited practices Wednesday and Thursday, Hockenson is ready to return against San Francisco in a potential playoff preview. His lack of a designation puts Minnesota's top tight end in position to reclaim his usual role in the passing game that now has Kirk Cousins at quarterback. Hockenson is a TE1 for fantasy purposes.
injuryReports.injury: Hockenson (wrist) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday night's game against the 49ers.

injuryReports.name: Eric Wilson
injuryReports.returnComment: The Vikings sacked Jordan Love eight times in Week 10, with Wilson taking down the Packers quarterback for a six-yard loss early in the second quarter. Wilson has logged at least 0.5 sacks in three of his last four outings, and the veteran linebacker is up to 57 tackles (30 solo), including 4.0 sacks, and one pass defense through nine regular-season games.
injuryReports.injury: Wilson recorded seven tackles (six solo), including 1.0 sacks, during the Vikings' 30-10 win over the Packers in Week 10.

injuryReports.name: Bo Richter
injuryReports.returnComment: Richter will now be forced to miss at least four games after suffering a foot injury during the Week 10 win over the Packers. The 26-year-old has compiled six tackles (three solo) across nine appearances this season while playing almost exclusively on special teams.
injuryReports.injury: Foot

injuryReports.name: Jauan Jennings
injuryReports.returnComment: Jennings sat out the last two games due to a calf injury, but his return to all activity Wednesday gives the Vikings' receiving corps a boost after Jordan Addison was lost for at least a few weeks due to a broken thumb that required surgery. As for Jennings, he'll have a prime opportunity to work opposite No. 1 WR Justin Jefferson as he looks to build upon his 6-54-0 line on 10 targets in his six appearances this season.
injuryReports.injury: Jennings (calf) practiced in full Wednesday.

injuryReports.name: Jay Ward
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable
injuryReports.injury: Knee

injuryReports.name: Jordan Addison
injuryReports.returnComment: Thus, the Vikings are expecting Addison to recover fully before the four games required of an IR stint, but in any case he will miss some time due to the thumb injury he suffered in practice last Friday and sidelined him this past Sunday at Green Bay. With Addison out of the lineup, Minnesota will be relying on Justin Jefferson, Jauan Jennings (calf), Myles Price, Tai Felton and Jeshaun Jones at wide receiver.
injuryReports.injury: Thumb

injuryReports.name: Will Reichard
injuryReports.returnComment: All three of Reichard's field goals came from fewer than 40 yards out in the contest. The return of Kirk Cousins allowed Minnesota's offense to surge to its highest touchdown total since Week 1, the team's first bout against the Packers. Reichard is now 23-for-25 on field-goal attempts and remains perfect at 13-for-13 on PATs over nine regular-season games in 2026.
injuryReports.injury: Reichard made all three of his field-goal attempts and all three PATs in the Vikings' 30-10 win over the Packers on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Myles Price
injuryReports.returnComment: Price reeled in a season-high four passes for 49 yards and a score during Sunday's 30-10 win over the Packers. The wideout was operating in a more prominent offensive role for the second week in a row with Jauan Jennings (calf) sidelined, and fellow wide receiver Jordan Addison (thumb) was unable to play as well. Addison now is expected to undergo thumb surgery, opening the door for Price to operate in an elevated position in Minnesota's offense for the time being.
injuryReports.injury: Price is set for an increase in offensive workload with Jordan Addison (thumb) sidelined, Kevin Seifert of ESPN.com reports.

injuryReports.name: Tai Felton
injuryReports.returnComment: Felton drew a start in Sunday's 30-10 win over the Packers, reeling in a season-high three of five targets for 33 yards over 56 offensive snaps. The wide receiver stepped into a starting role as a result of Jordan Addison (thumb) and Jauan Jennings (calf) being sidelined, and Addison is now reportedly set to undergo surgery to address his injury, opening the door for more opportunities for Felton moving forward.
injuryReports.injury: Felton is on track to operate in a more prominent role in Week 11 versus the 49ers, Kevin Seifert of ESPN.com reports.

injuryReports.name: Aaron Jones Sr.
injuryReports.returnComment: Jordan Mason led the Vikings with 59 rushing yards, but Jones had the more productive afternoon as he scored his first TD since Week 5 on a one-yard plunge in the second quarter. Jones' upside will remain limited while working in a timeshare with Mason, but he's still got some utility heading into a Week 11 clash with the 49ers.
injuryReports.injury: Jones carried the ball 11 times for 47 yards and a touchdown and caught his only target for eight yards in Sunday's 30-10 win over the Packers.

injuryReports.name: Jordan Mason
injuryReports.returnComment: The fifth-year RB led the Vikings in rushing yards, but Aaron Jones was the more productive player in the backfield, gaining 55 scrimmage yards on 12 touches and scoring on a one-yard plunge in the second quarter. Mason has yet to get into the end zone in four games since returning from a thumb injury, piecing together 182 rushing yards on 4.0 yards per carry while working in a timeshare with Jones. He could break that drought in Week 11 in a potential revenge game against the 49ers.
injuryReports.injury: Mason carried the ball 16 times for 59 yards and failed to catch his only target in Sunday's 30-10 win over the Packers.

injuryReports.name: Kirk Cousins
injuryReports.returnComment: Brought back to Minnesota at the trade deadline to stabilize the offense, Cousins did exactly that, connecting with Myles Price for a 38-yard TD in the first quarter and Gavin Bartholomew on a 20-yard score in the fourth while guiding Justin Jefferson to season highs in catches and targets. The Vikings' passing game didn't need to over-extend itself, however, as the defense sacked Jordan Love eight times in another dominant performance. Cousins may need to find another gear in Week 11 against the 49ers, but he'll have another week of practice to re-familiarize himself with Kevin O'Connell's scheme first.
injuryReports.injury: Cousins completed 21 of 31 passes for 207 yards and two touchdowns with one interception in Sunday's 30-10 win over the Packers. He added 11 rushing yards on three carries.

injuryReports.name: Justin Jefferson
injuryReports.returnComment: In Kirk Cousins' return to the Vikings, Jefferson led the team in catches, targets and receiving yards, although Myles Price and Gavin Bartholomew were on the other end of the QB's two touchdown passes. The nine grabs and 13 targets were season highs for Jefferson, while the yardage total was his best showing since Week 5. Despite a disappointing 40-467-4 line on 64 targets through eight games, the star wideout's outlook for the rest of the year is pointed up heading into a Week 11 clash with the 49ers.
injuryReports.injury: Jefferson caught nine of 13 targets for 74 yards in Sunday's 30-10 win over the Packers.

injuryReports.name: Joshua Metellus
injuryReports.returnComment: Metellus was added to the Vikings' practice report Friday due to a shoulder issue, but the injury won't prevent the seventh-year pro from suiting up for Sunday's NFC North showdown. He has 58 tackles (29 solo), including 0.5 sacks, and four pass defenses through eight regular-season games.
injuryReports.injury: Metellus (shoulder) is active for Sunday's game against the Packers.

injuryReports.name: Carson Wentz
injuryReports.returnComment: Kyler Murray (hamstring) is out for another week but may eventually replace Wentz as the No. 2 quarterback. Wentz's miserable performance against the Bills last week likely was a factor in the Vikings trading for Cousins.
injuryReports.injury: Wentz (ankle) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game at Green Bay, but Kirk Cousins will be Minnesota's starting quarterback.

injuryReports.name: DeeJay Dallas
injuryReports.returnComment: Dallas notched just eight offensive snaps but also contributed 19 snaps on special teams. The veteran running back went without a carry for the fourth time over Minnesota's past five games, indicating his lack of a role in the running game. Overall this season, Dallas has been a very small part of the Vikings' offense, recording four carries for 14 yards and five catches for 36 yards (on five targets) through eight contests.
injuryReports.injury: Dallas caught his only target for a two-yard gain in Monday's Week 9 loss to the Bills.

injuryReports.name: Phil Mafah
injuryReports.returnComment: It's the second time this season that Mafah has been promoted to the 53-man roster, with the first instance being Week 10 against the Eagles. His elevation gives the Giants another contributor on special teams and extra depth in the backfield behind Cam Skattebo, Devin Singletary and Greg Desrosiers.
injuryReports.injury: The Giants elevated Mafah from the practice squad to the active roster Saturday, Dan Salomone of the team's official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Isaiah Likely
injuryReports.returnComment: That said, Duggan noted that he did see Likely, who hasn't been on the Giants' Week 11 injury report so far, walking into the building after the team's Friday morning walkthrough. In any case, New York's upcoming practice report will provide context regarding Likely's apparent absence, as well as his official status for Sunday's game against the Jaguars.
injuryReports.injury: Likely (undisclosed) wasn't spotted at Friday's practice, Dan Duggan of The Athletic reports.

injuryReports.name: Malik Harrison
injuryReports.returnComment: Harrison missed the Giants' contest versus the Commanders in Week 10 because of a groin injury, but it appears he'll be able to return to game action in Week 11. Of his 141 total snaps so far in 2026, 136 have come on special teams.
injuryReports.injury: Harrison (groin) was a full participant at practice Thursday.

injuryReports.name: Jason Pinnock
injuryReports.returnComment: Pinnock left the Giants' game versus the Commanders in Week 10 with a back injury after just 15 defensive snaps, but it looks like he's back to full strength for Week 11. He should play a rotational role in the Giants' secondary during Sunday's contest against a run-heavy Jacksonville offense.
injuryReports.injury: Pinnock (back) was a full participant at practice Thursday.

injuryReports.name: Tyrone Tracy Jr.
injuryReports.returnComment: The Giants haven't provided any updates on Tracy since he landed on IR on Oct. 27 after sustaining a hamstring strain in a Week 7 win over the Texans, but the running back is seemingly progressing well and could be ready to play once he sits out the required four games. Once he's reinstated, Tracy could operate as a change-of-pace option behind Cam Skattebo, who appears to have reclaimed the lead role out of the New York backfield after a one-game benching in Week 6.
injuryReports.injury: Hamstring

injuryReports.name: Jameis Winston
injuryReports.returnComment: J.J. McCarthy made his third consecutive start for the Giants, but Winston continued to get sprinkled into the game plan during short-yardage situations. He extended a second-quarter drive that culminated in a Cam Skattebo touchdown by gaining a yard on a fourth-and-one play, but Winston was dropped for no gain on a third-and-one run in the fourth quarter that resulted in a Giants punt. The Giants may continue to turn to Winston for quarterback sneaks in future weeks in an effort to limit the wear and tear on McCarthy.
injuryReports.injury: Winston carried twice for one yard in Thursday's 24-21 loss to the Commanders.

injuryReports.name: Xavier Gipson
injuryReports.returnComment: Gipson will head to New York after spending the entirety of the 2026 campaign to this point on the Eagles' practice squad. The Giants waived primary kick and punt returner Charlie Jones on Monday, and Gipson will likely take over that role beginning in Week 11 against the Jaguars.
injuryReports.injury: Gipson was signed by the Giants off of Philadelphia's practice squad Monday, Pat Leonard of the New York Daily News reports.

injuryReports.name: Micah McFadden
injuryReports.returnComment: McFadden logged one tackle for loss in the contest. The starting inside linebacker assisted the Giants in holding the Commanders to 3.2 yards per carry and no rushing touchdowns in the game.
injuryReports.injury: McFadden made 10 tackles (five solo) in the Giants' 24-21 loss to the Commanders on Thursday.

injuryReports.name: Jevon Holland
injuryReports.returnComment: Holland picked off Jayden Daniels with 2:19 left in the fourth quarter, just one Commanders drive after Ar'Darius Washington picked the quarterback off. Despite back-to-back turnovers, the Giants' offense logged back-to-back three-and-outs to put the Commanders' offense in position to win the game.
injuryReports.injury: Holland logged three tackles (one solo) and one pass defensed for an interception in the Giants' 24-21 loss to the Commanders on Thursday.

injuryReports.name: Ar'Darius Washington
injuryReports.returnComment: Washington broke up two passes in the contest, picking off Jayden Daniels with 5:31 left in the fourth quarter of Thursday's game. Despite making a crucial play with the Giants up four points, the offense could not put more points on the board to cement a primetime win.
injuryReports.injury: Washington accumulated seven tackles (five solo) and two passes defensed, including one interception, in the Giants' 24-21 loss to the Commanders on Thursday.

injuryReports.name: Arvell Reese
injuryReports.returnComment: Reese led the Giants in tackles as a consistent force against the Commanders' run game in the NFC East showdown. Despite the rookie first-rounder's best efforts, the Giants allowed 24 points en route to a meaningful divisional loss.
injuryReports.injury: Reese logged 13 tackles (four solo) in the Giants' 24-21 loss to the Commanders on Thursday.

injuryReports.name: Dominic Zvada
injuryReports.returnComment: Zvada's miss was a chip-shot 33-yarder in the first quarter that sailed wide left. That proved to be a critical mistake, as the Commanders won by just three points. Zvada appeared to shore up his job security a bit by going 4-for-4 on FG tries in Week 9 against Philadelphia, but it's hard to ignore the fact that he's gone just 17-for-23 on field-goal attempts overall and has missed three kicks from under 50 yards. The rookie does have a perfect 16-for-16 mark on extra-point attempts, and head coach John Harbaugh expressed support for the inconsistent kicker Friday, saying of Zvada, "I'm confident that he's going to become a good kicker. If at some point and time it doesn't happen, it doesn't happen. But I'm not going to panic halfway through the season with a guy who has made a bunch of kicks," Dan Duggan of The Athletic reports.
injuryReports.injury: Zvada missed his only field-goal try and made all three of his PATs on Thursday in a loss to Washington.

injuryReports.name: Theo Johnson
injuryReports.returnComment: Johnson hasn't been able to get going in 2026, as he's finished with one or zero catches in six of his seven games so far. After working as New York's top tight end last season, he's been mostly an afterthought in the current campaign due to the arrival of Isaiah Likely, who went off for a 9-127-1 line on a team-leading 11 targets Thursday. As long as Likely is healthy, Johnson won't have much appeal in most fantasy formats.
injuryReports.injury: Johnson logged one catch (on three targets) for eight yards Thursday in a loss to the Commanders.

injuryReports.name: Darnell Mooney
injuryReports.returnComment: Mooney logged the third-most targets of any New York pass catcher, but he managed just two short receptions. Efficiency has been an issue for the veteran wideout throughout the campaign, as he's hauled in only 14 of 30 targets through nine contests. Mooney has finished with fewer than 10 yards in four of his past six appearances, so he's not a viable fantasy play at the moment.
injuryReports.injury: Mooney caught two of five targets for eight yards Thursday in a loss to Washington.

injuryReports.name: Devin Singletary
injuryReports.returnComment: Cam Skattebo came back from a hamstring injury and dominated backfield work, taking 21 touches for 122 yards and two touchdowns on an 88 percent snap share. Singletary played 92 percent of snaps the week before in a win at Philadelphia, but his 23 touches went for just 39 total yards and no TDs. It'll likely be another large workload for Skattebo when the Giants host the Jaguars in Week 11.
injuryReports.injury: Singletary played just five snaps on offense and took one carry for three yards in Thursday's 24-21 loss to the Commanders.

injuryReports.name: Malachi Fields
